articles.fullText:
Students from 22 universities across 14 countries gathered in a circle. One by one, they added their signatures to a banner that read, "I promise to speak only Chinese from today onward."
They spent nine weeks in Shanghai this summer, studying Mandarin and soaking up Chinese culture, as part of NYU Shanghai's annual Summer Chinese Immersion Program. There's just one rule: Speak only Mandarin.
Nearly 60 students joined the program, up 50% from last year.
"Nine weeks wasn't easy, but it was definitely worth it, and I hope to keep learning," said Faith Parker, a student from Virginia Commonwealth University.
The students' experience reflects a growing global interest in learning Mandarin. It is already the world's second most spoken language by total number of speakers. Here are four facts about Mandarin learning.
Fact one: Celebrity families are taking Mandarin seriously
Learning Mandarin is becoming increasingly common among celebrity children.
According to the ABC, US President Donald Trump's granddaughter, founder of SpaceX and CEO of Tesla Elon Musk's son, and the children of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg are also learning Mandarin Chinese.
British actress Rosamund Pike, who is well known for her fluent Chinese and deep understanding of and love for Chinese culture, chose her own Chinese name Pei Chunhua (裴淳华) years ago. "Chun" (淳) conveys sincerity and simplicity, while "Hua" (华) can refer to China as well as beauty and elegance.
During a visit to Shanghai with then British Prime Minister Keir Starmer in early 2026, she called Chinese "the language of the future," adding that learning Mandarin Chinese alongside English provides an interesting mental workout.
Founder of SpaceX and CEO of Tesla Elon Musk with his son at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, China, May 14, 2026. 
Fact two: 210 million people are learning Chinese globally
China's Center for Language Education and Cooperation reported in May that global Chinese learners had reached 210 million.
According to the global language database Ethnologue, Mandarin Chinese had 1.18 billion speakers worldwide in 2025, including 990 million native speakers and 194 million second-language speakers, cementing its place as a global language second only to English.
Mastering Mandarin isn't for the faint of heart, especially for those unfamiliar with Chinese characters and pinyin (phonetic transcription). But learners worldwide are putting in the work.
Proof of that is everywhere. The global scale of paid Chinese language proficiency tests (HSK) exploded 21-fold between 2004 and 2024. Annual participation reached 810,000 in 2025, bringing the cumulative number of test-takers to more than 8.5 million by the end of the year.
Pupils learn to write Chinese characters during a Chinese language class at a school in Moscow, Russia, February 14, 2025. 
Fact three: Mandarin is Duolingo's fastest-growing language in 12 countries
Duolingo's 2025 Language Report ranked Mandarin as the eighth most popular language on the platform worldwide.
Its appeal is growing across South America, Asia and Europe. In 12 countries, Mandarin was the fastest-growing language on the app in 2025, including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, France, Germany, Indonesia, Mexico, Poland, South Korea, Spain, Thailand and Türkiye.
It also claimed the spot as the second-fastest-growing language on Duolingo in the United States.
A Chinese class in Greater Jakarta, Indonesia, July 11, 2024. 
Fact four: Mandarin is making its way into classrooms worldwide
From the Middle East to Europe and the Americas, Mandarin is increasingly finding a home in the curriculum.
In the Middle East, data released by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Education in April 2025 showed that 174 public middle schools had introduced Mandarin courses. The country aims to have more than 600,000 middle and high school students learning the language by 2030.
In the UK, parliamentary data from July 2026 showed that 31% of state-funded secondary schools in England had at least one student taking GCSE Chinese in 2025. (GCSEs are standard academic qualifications taken by students in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland.)
In the United States, a 2026 report by the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) found that Chinese, including Mandarin and Cantonese, was taught in 6% of public high schools that offered foreign language courses.

articles.title: Why cling to zero-sum thinking in the age of AI?
articles.titleCn: 人工智能时代为何还要固守零和思维？
articles.summary: Why cling to zero-sum thinking in the age of AI?
articles.summaryCn: 文章指出，在人工智能深刻重塑生产力与文明的时代，一些国家仍以零和思维和集团对抗看待AI，通过技术限制与脱钩维护霸权，这不仅阻碍科技进步与全球治理，也忽视AI风险无国界、需各国合作应对的现实，中美作为AI大国应超越冷战思维，共同塑造技术未来。

paragraphs.en: Artificial intelligence is more than a technological upgrade. It is {{0}} productivity, social relations and civilization itself. How countries, particularly major AI powers, respond to this transformation will {{1}} influence its future. Yet some countries remain trapped in zero-sum thinking and bloc {{22}}, treating AI as a tool of great-power competition. Through technology restrictions, industrial decoupling and exclusive partnerships, they seek to preserve technological dominance and {{2}} the benefits of innovation.
paragraphs.cn: 人工智能不仅仅是一次技术升级。它正在重塑生产力、社会关系乃至文明本身。各国，尤其是主要人工智能大国，如何应对这一变革将深刻影响其未来。然而，一些国家仍陷于零和思维和集团对抗之中，将人工智能视为大国竞争的工具。它们通过技术限制、产业脱钩和排他性伙伴关系，试图维持技术主导地位并垄断创新收益。

paragraphs.en:
This outdated mindset is becoming a major {{3}} to technological progress and global AI governance. Artificial intelligence technology. Cooperation is key to innovation
History shows that openness and international cooperation have long driven scientific progress. The United States itself benefited from global talent flows and cross-border research {{4}} after World War II. China and the US also enjoyed productive periods of scientific exchange.
paragraphs.cn: 这种过时的心态正成为技术进步和全球人工智能治理的主要障碍。人工智能技术。合作是创新的关键。历史表明，开放和国际合作长期以来推动着科学进步。美国自身在二战后便受益于全球人才流动和跨境研究合作。中美两国也曾经历过富有成效的科学交流时期。

paragraphs.en: From early academic exchanges in the 1970s to joint research during the rise of deep learning, scholars and companies from both countries contributed to AI development. This history demonstrates that sharing knowledge can {{5}} innovation and benefit both sides. But cooperation has increasingly given way to strategic {{6}}. Washington has {{7}} restrictions on advanced chips, computing power and investment, framing technological competition as a national security issue. Such measures risk narrowing the space for long-term cooperation and {{8}} innovation, including within the United States itself.
paragraphs.cn: 从20世纪70年代的早期学术交流到深度学习兴起期间的联合研究，两国的学者和企业都为人工智能发展作出了贡献。这段历史表明，共享知识可以加速创新并使双方受益。但合作已日益让位于战略竞争。华盛顿收紧了针对先进芯片、算力和投资的限制，将技术竞争框定为国家安全问题。此类措施可能压缩长期合作的空间并削弱创新，包括美国自身的创新。

paragraphs.en:
AI poses challenges no country can tackle alone
The AI revolution is still in its early stages, and its future direction remains {{9}}. AI agents are becoming increasingly {{10}} of handling complex tasks, while advances in world models are pushing the technology toward a deeper understanding of the physical world. AI's {{11}} is also difficult to predict or control. Meanwhile, risks ranging from deepfakes and AI-enabled attacks to errors in {{12}} systems can cross borders. AI security is therefore not simply a national technological or industrial concern, but a {{13}} challenge facing all humanity.
paragraphs.cn: 人工智能带来的挑战没有哪个国家能独自应对。人工智能革命仍处于早期阶段，其未来走向仍不确定。AI智能体处理复杂任务的能力日益增强，而世界模型的进步正推动该技术更深入地理解物理世界。人工智能的演进也难以预测或控制。与此同时，从深度伪造和AI赋能攻击到自主系统错误等风险都可能跨越国界。因此，人工智能安全不仅仅是国家的技术或产业关切，而是全人类面临的系统性挑战。

paragraphs.en: At the opening of the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference, Chinese President Xi Jinping raised {{14}} questions about how humanity should coexist with increasingly capable machines, {{15}} security, keep governance {{16}} of technological change and ensure that AI's benefits are widely shared. These questions {{17}} the need for collective responses. Technological barriers may slow the spread of innovation, but they cannot stop AI's global development. Unilateral restrictions and {{18}} rules may instead create gaps in governance and increase systemic risks. The US and Chinese flag at the Great Hall of the People, Beijing, China, May 14, 2026.
paragraphs.cn: 在2026年世界人工智能大会开幕式上，中国国家主席习近平就人类应如何与能力日益强大的机器共存、保障安全、使治理跟上技术变革以及确保人工智能惠益广泛共享等根本性问题提出了疑问。这些问题凸显了集体应对的必要性。技术壁垒可能减缓创新的传播，但无法阻止人工智能的全球发展。单边限制和碎片化规则反而可能造成治理缺口并增加系统性风险。2026年5月14日，中国北京人民大会堂内的美国和中国国旗。

paragraphs.en:
China and the US have a shared responsibility
As two of the world's most {{19}} AI powers, China and the United States have a particular responsibility to shape the future of the technology. Competition is a natural part of innovation, but turning it into an ideological struggle risks {{20}} global progress and weakening the ability to address shared risks. The greater the uncertainty surrounding AI, the more important it is for major powers to exercise strategic {{21}}, uphold safeguards and expand opportunities for cooperation. The intelligent age requires a new strategic mindset—one that moves beyond Cold War-era confrontation. Countries need to develop shared understandings and governance approaches suited to the technology, setting rules through dialogue, strengthening {{23}} through openness and learning to coexist amid competition.

articles.fullText:
Artificial intelligence is more than a technological upgrade. It is reshaping productivity, social relations and civilization itself. How countries, particularly major AI powers, respond to this transformation will profoundly influence its future.
Yet some countries remain trapped in zero-sum thinking and bloc confrontation, treating AI as a tool of great-power competition. Through technology restrictions, industrial decoupling and exclusive partnerships, they seek to preserve technological dominance and monopolize the benefits of innovation. This outdated mindset is becoming a major obstacle to technological progress and global AI governance.
Artificial intelligence technology. 
Cooperation is key to innovation
History shows that openness and international cooperation have long driven scientific progress. The United States itself benefited from global talent flows and cross-border research collaboration after World War II.
China and the US also enjoyed productive periods of scientific exchange. From early academic exchanges in the 1970s to joint research during the rise of deep learning, scholars and companies from both countries contributed to AI development. This history demonstrates that sharing knowledge can accelerate innovation and benefit both sides.
But cooperation has increasingly given way to strategic rivalry. Washington has tightened restrictions on advanced chips, computing power and investment, framing technological competition as a national security issue. Such measures risk narrowing the space for long-term cooperation and undermining innovation, including within the United States itself.
AI poses challenges no country can tackle alone
The AI revolution is still in its early stages, and its future direction remains uncertain. AI agents are becoming increasingly capable of handling complex tasks, while advances in world models are pushing the technology toward a deeper understanding of the physical world.
AI's evolution is also difficult to predict or control. Meanwhile, risks ranging from deepfakes and AI-enabled attacks to errors in autonomous systems can cross borders. AI security is therefore not simply a national technological or industrial concern, but a systemic challenge facing all humanity.
At the opening of the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference, Chinese President Xi Jinping raised fundamental questions about how humanity should coexist with increasingly capable machines, safeguard security, keep governance abreast of technological change and ensure that AI's benefits are widely shared.
These questions underscore the need for collective responses. Technological barriers may slow the spread of innovation, but they cannot stop AI's global development. Unilateral restrictions and fragmented rules may instead create gaps in governance and increase systemic risks.
The US and Chinese flag at the Great Hall of the People, Beijing, China, May 14, 2026. 
China and the US have a shared responsibility
As two of the world's most influential AI powers, China and the United States have a particular responsibility to shape the future of the technology. Competition is a natural part of innovation, but turning it into an ideological struggle risks stifling global progress and weakening the ability to address shared risks.
The greater the uncertainty surrounding AI, the more important it is for major powers to exercise strategic restraint, uphold safeguards and expand opportunities for cooperation.
The intelligent age requires a new strategic mindset—one that moves beyond Cold War-era confrontation. Countries need to develop shared understandings and governance approaches suited to the technology, setting rules through dialogue, strengthening oversight through openness and learning to coexist amid competition.
AI should be a source of shared progress and human flourishing, not another instrument of division.
(Li Yan is director at the Institute of Science and Technology and Cybersecurity Studies at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations. CGTN reporter Li Shuang also contributed to the article.)

人工智能不仅仅是一次技术升级。它正在重塑生产力、社会关系乃至文明本身。各国，尤其是主要人工智能大国，如何应对这一变革将深刻影响其未来。然而，一些国家仍陷于零和思维和集团对抗之中，将人工智能视为大国竞争的工具。它们通过技术限制、产业脱钩和排他性伙伴关系，试图维持技术主导地位并垄断创新收益。

这种过时的心态正成为技术进步和全球人工智能治理的主要障碍。人工智能技术。合作是创新的关键。历史表明，开放和国际合作长期以来推动着科学进步。美国自身在二战后便受益于全球人才流动和跨境研究合作。中美两国也曾经历过富有成效的科学交流时期。

人工智能应成为共同进步和人类繁荣的源泉，而不是又一个分裂的工具。（李艳是中国现代国际关系研究院科技与网络安全研究所所长。CGTN记者李爽亦对本文有贡献。）

articles.fullText:
China will send a delegation to the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), scheduled for November 9 to 20 in Antalya, Türkiye, a Chinese official said Wednesday.
Li Gao, vice minister of ecology and environment, made the remarks at a press conference held by the State Council Information Office.
Li said China would actively advance international climate negotiations, describing the UN climate conference as the main channel and platform for international cooperation in addressing global climate change.
COP31 will conduct negotiations and consultations on nearly 100 agenda items related to the implementation of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement. These will cover areas including mitigation, adaptation, climate finance and just transition.
As global climate governance shifts its focus from negotiating rules to implementing commitments, China supports making implementation a key priority at COP31, Li said.
The conference should address longstanding issues, including insufficient emission reduction efforts and inadequate climate finance support from developed countries, as well as new challenges arising from unilateralism and protectionism that undermine collective global efforts to tackle climate change, he said.
The multilateral process should support all parties, particularly developing countries, and create favorable conditions for them to implement their nationally determined contributions (NDCs) and advance the goals of the Paris Agreement through concrete actions, Li said.
He called for consolidating political consensus on climate action through solidarity and cooperation, stressing that COP31 should uphold multilateralism, adhere to the objectives of the Convention and the Paris Agreement, and uphold the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.
The conference should send a clear political signal to the international community that the global transition toward green and low-carbon development is irreversible, he said.
Li also stressed the need to make progress on climate finance. He called for in-depth discussions at COP31 on a roadmap for developed countries to fulfill their commitment to providing $300 billion in climate finance by 2035, as well as the goal of tripling adaptation finance.
He further called for advancing international mechanisms for just transition to help countries, particularly developing countries, address the difficulties and challenges they face during the transition and narrow the gap between the Global North and the Global South.
China, as a responsible major developing country, has consistently participated in and advanced international climate negotiations in a proactive and constructive manner, contributing its wisdom, solutions and strength to the success of the conference, Li said.

articles.fullText:
Solar panels at a 100-megawatt photovoltaic project supporting a hydrogen energy industrial park in Gaolan County, Lanzhou, northwest China's Gansu Province, June 8, 2026. 
China has approved four-year pilot programs for comprehensive hydrogen energy applications in five city clusters, according to a government circular made public Friday.
The programs will cover the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, and three cross-regional groups linking northeast China, including eastern Inner Mongolia, with the Yangtze River Delta, Xinjiang with the Chengdu-Chongqing twin-city economic circle, and the Yellow River bend with the Central Plains.
The circular, jointly released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Finance and the National Development and Reform Commission, calls on participating cities to accelerate the implementation of four lists of priority tasks covering hydrogen technology and equipment development, industrial hydrogen projects, fuel cell vehicle promotion, and hydrogen refueling station construction.
Cities are also urged to strengthen industrial and supply chains, promote smooth domestic circulation and avoid local protectionism. The circular also calls for better planning of major projects, stronger safety management, and timely assessment of the pilot programs' economic, social and environmental benefits.
The three departments will assess the pilot programs, with the results serving as the basis for allocating central government reward funds. The funds must be disbursed promptly and used only to support hydrogen energy applications, helping lower hydrogen-use costs and pass the savings on to end users, according to the circular.
The initiative comes as China seeks to expand the use of cleaner energy in industry and transport. Hydrogen produced using renewable electricity can help reduce carbon emissions, although high costs and challenges in storage and transportation remain obstacles to wider adoption.
China is already the world's largest producer and consumer of hydrogen, with output exceeding 39 million tonnes in 2025, according to official data.
Under a policy issued in March, China aims to have 100,000 fuel cell vehicles nationwide by 2030, while each city cluster can receive up to 1.6 billion yuan (about $238 million) in central government reward funds over the four-year pilot period.

2026年6月8日，在中国西北部甘肃省兰州市皋兰县，一个支撑氢能产业园的100兆瓦光伏项目现场的太阳能电池板。根据周五公布的政府通知，中国已批准在五个城市群开展为期四年的氢能综合应用试点项目。这些项目将覆盖京津冀地区、粤港澳大湾区，以及三个连接东北地区（包括内蒙古东部）的跨区域组合——分别与长三角、新疆与成渝双城经济圈、黄河“几”字弯与中原地区。该通知由工业和信息化部、财政部和国家发展改革委联合发布，要求参与城市加快落实四张优先任务清单，涵盖氢能技术与装备研发、工业氢能项目、燃料电池汽车推广以及加氢站建设。通知还敦促各城市加强产业链和供应链，促进国内循环畅通，避免地方保护主义。通知还呼吁更好地规划重大项目、加强安全管理，并及时评估试点项目的经济、社会和环境效益。

三部门将对试点项目进行评估，评估结果将作为分配中央政府奖励资金的依据。根据通知，资金必须及时拨付，且只能用于支持氢能应用，帮助降低用氢成本并将节省下来的费用传递给终端用户。此举出台之际，中国正寻求在工业和交通领域扩大清洁能源的使用。利用可再生电力生产的氢能有助于减少碳排放，尽管高成本以及储运方面的挑战仍是更广泛应用的障碍。根据官方数据，中国已经是世界上最大的氢能生产国和消费国，2025年产量超过3900万吨。根据3月发布的一项政策，中国的目标是到2030年全国燃料电池汽车达到10万辆，而在四年试点期内，每个城市群最多可获得16亿元人民币（约合2.38亿美元）的中央政府奖励资金。

articles.fullText:
Posters promoting Türkiye's COP31 presidency is displayed outside Turkish House in New York, United States, September 21, 2026. 
China's permanent representative to the United Nations, Fu Cong, called on Friday for stronger global climate governance and an accelerated green and just transition.
Fu spoke at a high-level meeting titled "A Planet Fit for the Future: Restoring Trust through Climate Action," convened by the president of the UN General Assembly ahead of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31).
He urged the international community to stand united and accelerate action to achieve balanced, positive and practical outcomes at COP31.
Multilateral cooperation remains the most effective way to address climate challenges, Fu said. He called on countries to maintain their resolve and sustain their efforts to fully and effectively implement the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement.
Fu said countries should pursue a green and just transition along pathways suited to their national circumstances and resources, ensuring a just and orderly process. He urged stronger cooperation on critical minerals to build a fair, open, inclusive and mutually beneficial governance system that promotes environmentally sustainable practices and supports the energy transition.
Fu also called for greater support to strengthen developing countries' capacity for climate action. Developed countries should fulfill their climate commitments, while multilateral development banks and the private sector should increase climate investment and financing to help address gaps in funding, technology and capacity.
Countries should expand international cooperation on early warning systems, risk assessment, disaster prevention and mitigation, and improve mechanisms for rapid disbursement from the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage, he said.
China actively promotes and contributes to global climate action and has engaged in green cooperation with more than 100 countries and regions, Fu said.
China is ready to work with all parties to strengthen trust and cooperation through climate action and build a community with a shared future for humanity, he added.
